newsitem.title: GERMANY: Transrapid draws interest in Australia - Thyssen.
newsitem.headline: Transrapid draws interest in Australia - Thyssen.

text.p: The Australian government was showing increased interest in Germany's Transrapid magnetic levitation train for a high-speed rail line linking Sydney and Canberra, a German newspaper reported.
Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said he wanted to travel to Germany to ride the Transrapid test track in Emsland, the daily Sueddeutsche Zeitung said on Tuesday.
Sharp met with Transrapid consortium members as part of a visit by German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt.

Australia was considering several competing proposals for "tilt trains" that run on standard rails, but could also opt for more advanced technology, said Eckard Rohkamm, head of consortium member Thyssen Industrie AG.
The magnetic levitation train would be of much less interest to the Australians if Germany balked at building its own proposed Transrapid line between Hamburg and Berlin, Rohkamm said.
"The Australians naturally are counting on it that we build the Hamburg-Berlin," he said.
The 300 kilometer Sydney-Canberra trip would take 90 to 120 minutes on tilt-trains and about 60 minutes on the Transrapid.
Tilt train tickets were projected to cost less than $A60 $45.50). The Transrapid consortium, which also includes Siemens AG and ADtranz, has not yet given a projected cost for the project.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.315 Australian Dollars)
